policies.name: Payment Approver / Payment Processor
policies.description: The same user cannot both process and approve payments. This is the classic payment fraud scenario — a single identity controlling both sides of a financial transaction removes all maker-checker separation.
policies.compensating_control: Requires CISO and Finance Director sign-off. No exception permitted in regulated environments without documented board-level approval and quarterly access certification.

policies.name: IT User Provisioner / IT Access Approver
policies.description: The same user cannot both provision user accounts and approve the access those accounts receive. This eliminates maker-checker separation in the identity lifecycle — a single identity could create accounts and self-approve elevated access.
policies.compensating_control: Requires CISO sign-off. Role must be split across two distinct identities. No single-person exception permitted without documented compensating control reviewed quarterly.

policies.name: Payment Processor / Finance Auditor
policies.description: A user who can execute payment transactions cannot also audit their own activity. Audit independence is destroyed when the same identity can both initiate transactions and validate them during audit activities.
policies.compensating_control: Flag for governance review. Require written justification from Finance Director. Compensating control: enhanced transaction monitoring and independent quarterly audit review of all transactions processed by this identity.

policies.name: Payment Approver / Finance Auditor
policies.description: An auditor who also approves financial transactions loses independence. In regulated environments this constitutes a control failure — the identity responsible for validating financial accuracy cannot also be approving the transactions it reviews.
policies.compensating_control: Flag for governance review. Requires Finance Director and external audit liaison sign-off. This combination is typically disallowed in SOX and GDPR-regulated environments.

policies.name: Journal Poster / Finance Auditor
policies.description: A user who can post accounting journal entries cannot also audit and validate those entries. This allows an identity to manipulate accounting records and then certify them as accurate during audit activities.
policies.compensating_control: Flag for governance review. Compensating control: all journal entries posted by this identity must be independently reviewed by a second Finance team member before audit sign-off. Requires Finance Director approval.

policies.name: HR Salary Admin / HR Data Export
policies.description: A user who can administer salary and payroll data cannot also bulk export sensitive employee information. This combination presents a direct insider data exfiltration risk — a single identity can access and extract the organisation's most sensitive HR records.
policies.compensating_control: Requires HR Director and DPO sign-off. Compensating control: all data export activity by this identity must be logged, monitored via DLP policy, and reviewed monthly. Export volumes must be reported to the DPO quarterly.
